{"body":"## Summary

Rich, range-styled text for Pathland: an **`AttributedString`** model, inline-**Markdown** parsing, transmitted as a structured arena payload via a new **`STYLE::SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT`** command, and rendered natively on every surface (GTK/pango, SSR HTML, DOM client).

The 16-byte opcode is untouched — all variable-length data (text + runs) lives in the **arena** as one length-prefixed entry, referenced by offset. This mirrors how `SET_TEXT` works today.

## Design

### Wire: `STYLE::SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT` (0x04)

`A=nodeId, B=arenaRef (payload), C=0`.

Arena payload (one `[u32 byteLength][bytes]` entry):

```
[ u32 textLen ][ utf8 text ]
[ u32 styleRunCount ][ style runs... ]
[ u32 linkCount ][ links... ]
```

- **Tagged style run**: `(u32 start)(u32 end)(u8 count) ((u16 propId)(4-byte value)) × count` — reuses the existing text-format property vocabulary (`FONT_SIZE` 0x1007, `FONT_WEIGHT` 0x1008, `FONT_STYLE` 0x1017, `FONT_DESIGN` 0x1018, `COLOR` 0x100A, `UNDERLINE`, `STRIKETHROUGH`, …); values use the standard encodings (F32/enum LE, packed ARGB, U8). Node-level properties remain the base; runs override ranges.
- **Link**: `(u32 start)(u32 end)(u8 urlLen)(utf8 url)` — links are a separate section so style runs stay 4-byte-valued only.

### Shared Markdown parser (one parser for every DSL)

New `no_std` + `alloc` crate **`pathland-markdown`**: parses an inline subset —

- `**bold**`, `*italic*`, `` `code` ``, `~~strikethrough~~`, `[link](url)`

— into the AttributedString/payload. Used natively by the Rust DSL; exported as a **cdylib C ABI** and bound by Java via **JNA** (embedded in a shim jar, the `pathland-render-html` pattern) so `Markdown.parse(...)` shares the exact same parser across all DSLs. (Consequence: Java markdown parsing adds a native dependency; the `AttributedString` *builder* stays pure Java.)

### DSL surface

- **Java**: `AttributedString` builder (range-tracking fluent builder), `Text.of(AttributedString)`, `Markdown.parse(String)` (JNA).
- **Rust** (`pathland-view`): the same builder + parser, natively.
- **Fine-grained**: `Text.of(Signal<AttributedString>)` re-emits `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT` only when the encoded payload changes (zero opcodes when unchanged).

### Renderers

- **GTK4** (`pathland-render-gtk`): build one `pango::AttrList` from the runs — `AttrWeight`, `AttrStyle`, `AttrSize`, `AttrForeground`, … plus **`PANGO_ATTR_LINK`** for link runs — set on the `GtkLabel`.
- **SSR HTML** (`pathland-render-html`): emit the text as nested styled `<span>` runs (reusing the existing inline-style mapping) and `<a href>` for links.
- **DOM client** (`@pathland/dom-renderer`): hydrate the SSR spans; apply deltas surgically with **`document.createRange()` + `splitText`/`surroundContents`** (wrap only the changed character range in a styled span; full rebuild only for wholesale payload changes). `Range` is browser-only — SSR still emits spans.

### Conformance

Golden byte vectors for `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT` and the arena payload (`spec/CONFORMANCE.md`); cross-renderer mapping tests; per-project `status.md` updates.

## Phases

1. **Protocol + core**: `spec/OPCODE.md` (command + arena payload), `spec/MODIFIERS.md`/`spec/PRIMITIVES.md` (text/attribute notes), `pathland-core` encode/decode, `CONFORMANCE.md` vectors.
2. **Shared parser**: `pathland-markdown` crate + cdylib C ABI + Java JNA shim.
3. **DSLs**: Rust + Java `AttributedString` builders, `Text.of(AttributedString)`, `Markdown.parse`, signal bindings.
4. **Renderers**: GTK pango, SSR HTML spans, DOM client `createRange` deltas.
5. **Tests + status.md** across all implementing projects.

## Constraints

- Protocol-first: spec + conformance vectors before implementation.
- Fixed 16-byte opcodes (the payload is arena-only).
- `no_std` core; zero dynamic allocation in steady-state emission.
- Stateless renderers: the run tree is a pure function of the opcode stream.
","comments":[],"labels":[],"number":98,"title":"AttributedString + inline Markdown: rich text end-to-end (protocol → shared parser → DSLs → renderers)"}

---

## Command Tables

### TREE (0x01)

The `componentType` values (the primitive views the protocol supports) are
catalogued in [PRIMITIVES.md](./PRIMITIVES.md), grouped by their SwiftUI
counterpart. Component IDs are allocated there spec-first; this file remains
the wire-format authority.

| Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | Description |
|---------|-------|---|---|---|-------|-------------|
| `CREATE_NODE` | `0x01` | nodeId | componentType (u16, low) | 0 | — | Create a node of `componentType` |
| `DELETE_NODE` | `0x02` | nodeId | 0 | 0 | — | Delete a node and its subtree |
| `INSERT_CHILD` | `0x03` | parentId | childId | index | — | Insert `childId` into `parentId` at `index`; append is `index = u32::MAX` (`APPEND`) |
| `REMOVE_CHILD` | `0x04` | parentId | childId | 0 | — | Remove `childId` from `parentId` |
| `MOVE_CHILD` | `0x05` | parentId | childId | newIndex | — | Move child to `newIndex` (after removal); append is `newIndex = u32::MAX` (`APPEND`) |

### PARAMETER (0x02)

The engine does not emit positions. `PARAMETER` carries the **constraint properties**
that native renderers feed to their own layout — spacing, alignment, FILL/HUG
size hints — plus **styling modifiers** (padding, colors, fonts, borders).

| Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | Description |
|---------|-------|---|---|---|-------|-------------|
| `SET_PROPERTY` | `0x01` | nodeId | propertyId (u16, low) + valueType (u8, high byte) | value | — | Set a constraint/style property; `value` depends on `valueType` |
| `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` | `0x02` | arenaRef (path) | valueType (u8) | value | — | Override a design token; path is an arena string |
| `SET_TEXT` | `0x03` | nodeId | arenaRef (utf8) | 0 | — | Set a node's text content |
| `SET_DATE` | `0x04` | nodeId | days since epoch (I32) | millis of day (U32) | — | Set a node's date value (e.g. a `DATE_PICKER`); see [EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md#date) for the matching `DATE_CHANGED` event |

`SET_PROPERTY` encodes the value type in the **high byte of `B`** (bits 24–31) and the property id in the low two bytes:

```
B = (valueType << 16) | propertyId
```

#### Value types

| Value Type | Value | C / value encoding |
|------------|-------|--------------------|
| `U8` | `0x01` | low byte of C |
| `U32` | `0x02` | u32 |
| `I32` | `0x03` | i32 |
| `F32` | `0x04` | f32 |
| `STRING` | `0x05` | arenaRef (utf8) |
| `ENUM` | `0x06` | low byte of C |
| `COLOR` | `0x07` | packed `0xAARRGGBB` |
| `DESIGN_TOKEN` | `0x08` | arenaRef (token path) |
| `LIST` | `0x09` | arenaRef (length-prefixed array, see below) |

> **Enum-valued properties** (`ALIGNMENT`, `TEXT_ALIGNMENT`, `TRUNCATION_MODE`,
> `ROLE`, `STATE`, and the draft `FONT_*`/`CONTENT_MODE`/`CONTROL_SIZE`/`SHAPE_KIND`
> properties) are carried with the **`F32` value type**, holding the numeric enum
> code as an f32 bit pattern (e.g. `ALIGNMENT=Center(1)` → `C = 1.0f32.to_bits()`).
> The enumerated code tables live in
> [MODIFIERS.md](./MODIFIERS.md#appendix-enumerated-values). The `ENUM` value type
> (low byte of `C`) is available for explicitly `ENUM`-coded properties.
>
> **Token references**: any property that normally carries a `COLOR` / `F32` /
> `STRING` / `ENUM` value MAY instead carry the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type, with
> `C` = arenaRef to a token path (see [Design Token System](#design-token-system)
> and [TOKENS.md](./TOKENS.md)).
>
> **`LIST` arrays**: a `LIST` value (`C` = arenaRef) is a length-prefixed array in
> the string arena: `[u32 count][element × count]`, each element a `u32` holding
> the value-type's bit pattern — currently produced with each element a `F32`
> (the `FIT_QUERY` threshold table), so `bytes = 4 + 4·count`. The count is the
> first `u32` (little-endian); a zero count is an empty list. Decoders read the
> element count, never infer it from the arena length, so a property can re-emit
> a shorter list with the arena entry intact.

#### Constraint properties for native layout

The following properties drive native layout; the renderer maps them to its
native layout properties (e.g. `SPACING` → a gap between children,
`WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` → size requests). Special `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` values: `-1` = FILL
(expand to available), `-2` = HUG_CONTENT (native intrinsic size).

> **Allocation semantics** — the exact meaning of a Fixed / `FILL` / `HUG_CONTENT`
> size, how containers distribute space to children (main axis: only `FILL`
> expands; cross axis: children hug unless `FILL`), and how content fits inside
> a Fixed box, are defined in [LAYOUT.md](./LAYOUT.md).

> **Units — logical points.** All size properties (`WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`/`SPACING`/
> `PADDING`/`CONTENT_MARGINS`, …) are expressed in an abstract **logical point**
> unit — the same abstraction as SwiftUI points, Jetpack Compose `dp`, and CSS
> pixels. A renderer MUST allocate the requested points box and fit content
> within it; it must never treat the value as a device-pixel size. Each renderer
> maps points to its native unit and resolves its own device resolution (logical
> points × scale factor), so the same value yields the same physical size across
> renderers.

| Property | Value | Type | Native meaning |
|----------|-------|------|----------------|
| `SPACING` | `0x0001` | F32 | Gap between children |
| `ALIGNMENT` | `0x0002` | F32 (enum code) | Cross-axis position (never stretches; default = Leading, `Fill`(3) = default hug — see LAYOUT.md) |
| `CONTENT_MARGINS` | `0x0005` | F32 | Uniform inset between a stack's edge and its content |
| `WIDTH` | `0x100B` | F32 | Width hint (-1 FILL, -2 HUG) |
| `HEIGHT` | `0x100C` | F32 | Height hint (-1 FILL, -2 HUG) |
| `GRID_COLUMNS` | `0x001E` | F32 | Grid column count (positive = count, -1/absent = auto-fit; a count, never a pixel width — see PRIMITIVES.md §Grid) |
| `GRID_ROWS` | `0x001F` | F32 | Grid row count (positive = count, -1/absent = auto-fit) |
| `GRID_TRACKS` | `0x0020` | STRING | Per-track grid spec (`flex`/`fixed:<pts>`/`adaptive:<pts>`, comma-separated) — takes precedence over the counts |

#### Text properties

Text-bearing nodes (`TEXT`, `BUTTON` labels, `TEXT_FIELD`) carry their content
via `SET_TEXT` (0x03) and their layout via these properties:

| Property | Value | Type | Native meaning |
|----------|-------|------|----------------|
| `TEXT` | `0x000A` | STRING | The text content (a `SET_TEXT`-style arena string) |
| `LINE_LIMIT` | `0x000B` | U32 | Maximum number of lines (0 = unlimited) |
| `TEXT_ALIGNMENT` | `0x000C` | F32 (enum code) | Alignment of the text block within its bounds |
| `TRUNCATION_MODE` | `0x000D` | F32 (enum code) | Truncation style when text overflows (`Head`/`Middle`/`Tail`) |

Enumerated values for these and every other enum-valued property are
consolidated in [MODIFIERS.md](./MODIFIERS.md#appendix-enumerated-values).

#### Styling properties (modifiers)

Styling properties are **modifiers** — they apply to any view, not just stacks —
and map to visual decoration rather than layout. `PADDING` (uniform) and its
per-edge variants map to native padding, alongside
`COLOR`/`BACKGROUND_COLOR`/`BORDER_*`:

|----------|-------|------|----------------|

#### Window metadata

`META::SET_WINDOW_METADATA` is an **extensible field family** for presentation
metadata of the host **window/surface** that owns the stream (a browser tab, a
native window, an embedded surface). One opcode sets one field; new fields are
new ids, never new commands. The protocol defines the concept; **each renderer
maps it onto its own chrome** — the browser mapping is only one of them:

| Renderer | `TITLE` | `DESCRIPTION` | `LOCALE` |
|----------|---------|---------------|----------|
| HTML / SSR | `<title>` | `<meta name="description">` | `<html lang>` |
| DOM client | `document.title` | meta description | `<html lang>` |
| GTK4 | window/headerbar title | accessible description | — |
| Qt | window title | — | — |

| Field | Value | `B` encoding | Notes |
|-------|-------|--------------|-------|
| `TITLE` | `0x0001` | string offset | Title of the hosting window/surface |
| `DESCRIPTION` | `0x0002` | string offset | Human-readable description of the current content |
| `LOCALE` | `0x0003` | string offset | BCP 47 content locale |

The string encoding follows the same convention as `SET_TEXT`/`ROUTE`: an
absolute offset into the guest arena over the shared ring, or a *relative*
offset into the batch's string section over the network. An **empty string
clears** the field, and the renderer applies its own default. Metadata is
renderer-global (not part of the retained tree), survives `META::RESET`, and is
re-emitted in a full snapshot (`META::RESYNC`).

Semantics:

- The application owns the values; a bound signal change emits exactly the
  changed field (like a property diff).
- A proxied origin's window metadata is **ignored** — an embedded app never
  retitles the host window (spec/PROXY.md).
- Web-only artifacts (`canonical`, `robots`, sitemap) are host concerns and are
  **not** protocol fields.

## Reactive Emission

The engine emits **only what changed** relative to its previous emission:

- **Property diff**: a changed `spacing`/`padding`/`WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`/`ALIGNMENT`/
  text emits a single `SET_PROPERTY` / `SET_TEXT` for that node. (Padding is a
  styling modifier, but it still diffs and emits like any other property.)
- **Structural diff**: a node added/removed/moved emits the corresponding
  `TREE` opcode(s).
- **Steady state**: an unchanged tree emits **zero** opcodes.

The **`frame` compound modifier** (width/height/alignment) is not a distinct
protocol concept: it emits `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`/`ALIGNMENT` as ordinary
`PARAMETER:SET_PROPERTY` deltas, exactly like any other constraint property. There
is no `frame` opcode or dedicated wire type.

Signals in the application drive this: a signal marks the tree dirty; the
engine's next `emit` reconciles and writes only the delta. The renderer applies
each frame as a delta to its native elements.

---

## Linear Memory Layout

The guest engine and host share a **single linear memory**. Regions are fixed at module start:

```
+───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────+
| 0x0000  Header block (80 B)  — cursors, frame counter, layout  |
| 0x0050  Ring buffer (16 B × slotCount)   [guest → host]        |
| ...      (slots densely packed, 64-byte aligned base)          |
| 0x10050 Event ring buffer (16 B × slotCount) [host → guest]    |
| ...                                                           |
| 0x20050 Arena (bump region, guest-owned: strings / tokens)     |
| ...                                                           |
| 0x30050 Event arena (bump region, host-owned: event strings)   |
| ...                                                            |
+───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────+
```

> The event ring is the **host → guest** direction of the shared-memory
> transport: the renderer writes `EVENT`-category opcodes here and the
> guest/app drains them. It uses the same 16-byte slot layout as the main
> (guest → host) ring; both share `slotCount` (same capacity).
>
> The **event arena** is the host-owned bump region that makes strings flow
> **host → guest** over the shared ring: a renderer bump-allocates `TEXT_CHANGED`
> text (and any future string-bearing event payload) here and references it by
> its absolute byte offset — exactly mirroring how the guest uses the guest
> arena for `SET_TEXT` / STRING properties. The host resets its cursor on
> `META::RESET`; if the event arena is full the host applies backpressure
> (drops/stalls the event), mirroring ring backpressure.

| 0x0A | 4 | `ringBytes` | — | Byte length of the ring region |
| 0x0E | 4 | `slotCount` | — | Number of ring slots (power of two) |
| 0x12 | 4 | `arenaOffset` | — | Byte offset of the arena region |
| 0x16 | 4 | `arenaBytes` | — | Byte length of the arena region |
| 0x1A | 4 | `arenaCursor` | guest | Next free byte in the arena |
| 0x1E | 4 | `readCursor` | host | Ring slot the host has consumed up to |
| 0x22 | 4 | `writeCursor` | guest | Ring slot the guest has written up to |
| 0x26 | 4 | `frameCount` | guest | Monotonic completed-frame counter |

| 0x2E | 4 | `eventRingBytes` | — | Byte length of the event ring region |

| 0x36 | 4 | `eventReadCursor` | guest | Event ring slot the guest has consumed up to |
| 0x3A | 4 | `eventWriteCursor` | host | Event ring slot the host has written up to |

### Ring buffer

- Contiguous array of **16-byte slots**; `slotCount` is a **power of two** (wrap via mask, no modulo).
- **Producer** (guest) writes at `writeCursor`, then advances `writeCursor` and increments `frameCount` at frame end.
- **Consumer** (host) reads from `readCursor` up to `writeCursor`; after draining a frame it advances `readCursor`.
- **Backpressure**: the producer must not advance `writeCursor` past `readCursor` (ring full). The producer SHOULD flush a frame before the ring is full.
- **Frame boundary detection**: the host watches `frameCount`. When it advances, exactly one frame (all slots from the previously consumed `readCursor` to the current `writeCursor`) is complete.

### Event ring (host → guest)

- The **host** (renderer) is the producer: it writes `EVENT`-category opcodes at `eventWriteCursor`.
- The **guest** (app/engine) is the consumer: it reads from `eventReadCursor` up to `eventWriteCursor`, then advances `eventReadCursor`.
- Events are raw inputs and are consumed as soon as they are written (no frame batching); `eventFrameCount` is not required.
- Backpressure mirrors the main ring: the host must not advance `eventWriteCursor` past `eventReadCursor`.

### Arena

- A pre-allocated **bump region** for variable-length data (strings, token paths).
- Every arena entry is **self-describing**: `[u32 byteLength][bytes...]`.
- Opcodes reference entries by their **byte offset** (`arenaRef`), so an entry's length is read directly from the arena — all opcodes stay 16 bytes.
- The guest advances `arenaCursor` monotonically (no free-list, no fragmentation). The arena MAY be reset via `META::RESET`.

### Event arena (host → guest)

The event arena is the **host-owned mirror** of the arena, giving the shared-memory
transport a host → guest string section so strings flow **both ways on all
transports**:

- The **host** (renderer) bump-allocates event string payloads here (e.g. the
  new text of a `TEXT_CHANGED`) and references them by their **absolute byte
  offset** in the event opcode — the same `SET_TEXT` shared-memory convention
  used in the guest arena.
- The **guest** resolves the text from the event arena region when draining
  events (`EVENT::TEXT_CHANGED`).
- Entries share the same self-describing `[u32 byteLength][bytes...]` layout as
  the guest arena.
- The host advances `eventArenaCursor` monotonically and resets it on
  `META::RESET`; a full event arena is backpressure (the host drops/stalls the
  event until the guest drains or a reset lands).
- Over the **network**, host → guest string payloads use the batch's string
  section with *relative* offsets instead (see [Transport](#transport)) — the
  same dual absolute/relative convention as `SET_TEXT`.

---

## Colors

Literal colors are **sRGB** (IEC 61966-2-1, D65 white point), packed as `0xAARRGGBB`:

- `AA`: alpha (0x00 transparent – 0xFF opaque)
- `RR`: red, `GG`: green, `BB`: blue

Stored little-endian in a `u32` payload. A color **property** may alternatively carry a `DESIGN_TOKEN` reference to a token path instead of a literal (see [Design Token System](#design-token-system)); semantic token resolution and theme adaptation remain **renderer-owned**.

| ...      (slots densely packed, 64-byte aligned base)          |
| 0x10050 Event ring buffer (16 B × slotCount) [host → guest]    |
| ...                                                           |
| 0x20050 Arena (bump region, guest-owned: strings / tokens)     |
| ...                                                           |
| 0x30050 Event arena (bump region, host-owned: event strings)   |
| ...                                                            |
+───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────+
```

> The event ring is the **host → guest** direction of the shared-memory
> transport: the renderer writes `EVENT`-category opcodes here and the
> guest/app drains them. It uses the same 16-byte slot layout as the main
> (guest → host) ring; both share `slotCount` (same capacity).
>
> The **event arena** is the host-owned bump region that makes strings flow
> **host → guest** over the shared ring: a renderer bump-allocates `TEXT_CHANGED`
> text (and any future string-bearing event payload) here and references it by
> its absolute byte offset — exactly mirroring how the guest uses the guest
> arena for `SET_TEXT` / STRING properties. The host resets its cursor on
> `META::RESET`; if the event arena is full the host applies backpressure
> (drops/stalls the event), mirroring ring backpressure.

### Header block (80 bytes)

| Offset | Size | Field | Producer | Description |
|--------|------|-------|----------|-------------|
| 0x00 | 4 | `magic` | — | `0x504C504C` (`PLPL`) |
| 0x04 | 2 | `version` | — | Wire protocol version (1) |
| 0x06 | 4 | `ringOffset` | — | Byte offset of the ring region |
| 0x0A | 4 | `ringBytes` | — | Byte length of the ring region |
| 0x0E | 4 | `slotCount` | — | Number of ring slots (power of two) |
| 0x12 | 4 | `arenaOffset` | — | Byte offset of the arena region |
| 0x16 | 4 | `arenaBytes` | — | Byte length of the arena region |
| 0x1A | 4 | `arenaCursor` | guest | Next free byte in the arena |
| 0x1E | 4 | `readCursor` | host | Ring slot the host has consumed up to |
| 0x22 | 4 | `writeCursor` | guest | Ring slot the guest has written up to |
| 0x26 | 4 | `frameCount` | guest | Monotonic completed-frame counter |
| 0x2A | 4 | `eventRingOffset` | — | Byte offset of the host→guest event ring region |
| 0x2E | 4 | `eventRingBytes` | — | Byte length of the event ring region |
| 0x32 | 4 | `eventSlotCount` | — | Event ring slot count (power of two; = `slotCount`) |
| 0x36 | 4 | `eventReadCursor` | guest | Event ring slot the guest has consumed up to |
| 0x3A | 4 | `eventWriteCursor` | host | Event ring slot the host has written up to |
| 0x40 | 4 | `eventArenaOffset` | — | Byte offset of the host→guest event arena region |
| 0x44 | 4 | `eventArenaBytes` | — | Byte length of the event arena region |
| 0x48 | 4 | `eventArenaCursor` | host | Next free byte in the event arena |

### Ring buffer

- Contiguous array of **16-byte slots**; `slotCount` is a **power of two** (wrap via mask, no modulo).
- **Producer** (guest) writes at `writeCursor`, then advances `writeCursor` and increments `frameCount` at frame end.
- **Consumer** (host) reads from `readCursor` up to `writeCursor`; after draining a frame it advances `readCursor`.
- **Backpressure**: the producer must not advance `writeCursor` past `readCursor` (ring full). The producer SHOULD flush a frame before the ring is full.
- **Frame boundary detection**: the host watches `frameCount`. When it advances, exactly one frame (all slots from the previously consumed `readCursor` to the current `writeCursor`) is complete.

### Event ring (host → guest)

- The **host** (renderer) is the producer: it writes `EVENT`-category opcodes at `eventWriteCursor`.
- The **guest** (app/engine) is the consumer: it reads from `eventReadCursor` up to `eventWriteCursor`, then advances `eventReadCursor`.
- Events are raw inputs and are consumed as soon as they are written (no frame batching); `eventFrameCount` is not required.
- Backpressure mirrors the main ring: the host must not advance `eventWriteCursor` past `eventReadCursor`.

### Arena

- A pre-allocated **bump region** for variable-length data (strings, token paths).
- Every arena entry is **self-describing**: `[u32 byteLength][bytes...]`.
- Opcodes reference entries by their **byte offset** (`arenaRef`), so an entry's length is read directly from the arena — all opcodes stay 16 bytes.
- The guest advances `arenaCursor` monotonically (no free-list, no fragmentation). The arena MAY be reset via `META::RESET`.

### Event arena (host → guest)

The event arena is the **host-owned mirror** of the arena, giving the shared-memory
transport a host → guest string section so strings flow **both ways on all
transports**:

- The **host** (renderer) bump-allocates event string payloads here (e.g. the
  new text of a `TEXT_CHANGED`) and references them by their **absolute byte
  offset** in the event opcode — the same `SET_TEXT` shared-memory convention
  used in the guest arena.
- The **guest** resolves the text from the event arena region when draining
  events (`EVENT::TEXT_CHANGED`).
- Entries share the same self-describing `[u32 byteLength][bytes...]` layout as
  the guest arena.
- The host advances `eventArenaCursor` monotonically and resets it on
  `META::RESET`; a full event arena is backpressure (the host drops/stalls the
  event until the guest drains or a reset lands).
- Over the **network**, host → guest string payloads use the batch's string
  section with *relative* offsets instead (see [Transport](#transport)) — the
  same dual absolute/relative convention as `SET_TEXT`.

---

## Colors

Literal colors are **sRGB** (IEC 61966-2-1, D65 white point), packed as `0xAARRGGBB`:

- `AA`: alpha (0x00 transparent – 0xFF opaque)
- `RR`: red, `GG`: green, `BB`: blue

Stored little-endian in a `u32` payload. A color **property** may alternatively carry a `DESIGN_TOKEN` reference to a token path instead of a literal (see [Design Token System](#design-token-system)); semantic token resolution and theme adaptation remain **renderer-owned**.

                <executions>

                        <phase>process-test-sources</phase>

                        <configuration>

                            </sourceDirs>
                        </configuration>
                    </execution>

                                <copy file="${pathland.native.host}"

                            </target>
                        </configuration>
                        <goals>
                            <goal>run</goal>
                        </goals>
                    </execution>
                </executions>
            </plugin>

Now, I need to produce the plan. But first maybe verify the exact `AttributedString` design layout. Let me think more carefully about a robust wire format that is easy to implement across Rust/Java/TS.

### Proposed payload format (v1)

The arena/string-section entry is already `[u32 byteLength][bytes]`. Inside:

```
[u32 text_byte_len][utf8 text]
[u32 run_count]
  run:
    [u32 start][u32 end][u32 attr_count]
    attr:
      [u16 prop_id][u8 value_type][u8 reserved][u32 value]
[u32 link_count]
  link:
    [u32 start][u32 end][u32 url_byte_len][utf8 url]
```

Use little-endian. Ranges are UTF-8 byte offsets into text, `start <= end <= text_byte_len`, both on char boundaries. `value_type` is the standard `ValueTypes` code; `value` is the 4-byte encoded value (U8/U32/I32/F32/ENUM/COLOR). DESIGN_TOKEN/STRING/LIST are invalid in runs in v1 (no nested arena). This is a deviation from issue's 6-byte attr; justify: deterministic value typing, forward compatibility, 4-byte alignment. Or keep the issue's format but add value type. I think this is good.

Alternatively, use `[u16 prop_id][u16 value_type]`? Value type only needs u8. Fine.

Run attr count u32. Style run counts u32. Link URL len u32.

Edge cases:
- Duplicate attr in a run: last wins.
- Overlapping runs: for each segment, apply covering runs in wire order; later run's attr wins.
- Link overlap: last covering link wins (or first? define last).
- Empty text + runs invalid (ranges must be within text).
- No runs/links => equivalent to SET_TEXT, but still valid.
- Bounds-checked decode, no panics; invalid payload leaves text unset / ignores opcode (renderer must not crash). Log in debug.

### Node model

`AttributedString`:
```rust
pub struct AttributedString {
    text: String,
    runs: Vec<StyleRun>,
    links: Vec<LinkRun>,
}
pub struct StyleRun { start: usize, end: usize, attrs: Vec<(u16, Value)> }
pub enum Value { U8(u8), U32(u32), I32(i32), F32(f32), Color(u32) } // or raw u32 + value type
pub struct LinkRun { start, end, url: String }
```
Need `no_std` and `alloc`. Perhaps store `Vec<(u16, u8, u32)>` internally, with typed constructors. `PartialEq` derives.

Encoding/decoding in `pathland-core/src/attributed.rs`, with tests and fuzz/bounds tests.

Java `AttributedString` mirrors with Kotlin data classes and a builder:
```kotlin
class AttributedString(val text: String, val runs: List<StyleRun>, val links: List<LinkRun>)
class AttributedStringBuilder { fun append(text); fun bold(start,end); fun italic(...); fun foreground(start,end,color); ... fun link(start,end,url); fun build() }
```
Maybe builder maintains a current text buffer and allows range methods by offsets. `Markdown.parse` returns `AttributedString`.

  layout-transparent) owns the resource + transport; a `VIDEO` (`0x0A`) surface
  references it via `MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID` (`0x103A`). Transport properties
  `PLAYBACK_STATE` (0x1035), `MEDIA_POSITION` (0x1036), `MEDIA_VOLUME` (0x1037),
  `MEDIA_SOURCE` (0x103B), `MEDIA_MUTED` (0x103C), `MEDIA_LOOP` (0x103D),
  `MEDIA_RATE` (0x103E); the `MEDIA_*` events target the **controller** id and add
  `MEDIA_DURATION_CHANGED` (0x14). Covered by conformance vectors 39–41.

I could not create the branch because plan mode is read-only; step 0 below runs after approval. I also confirmed issue #98 is the rich-text issue, not a website task.

### Decisions locked in
- **Branch:** `feat/attributed-string-markdown` off `main`.
- **Command ID:** `PARAMETER::SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT = 0x05` (not `0x04`; `SET_DATE` already owns `0x04`). A separate follow-up issue will cover regrouping the PARAMETER command IDs.
- **Links:** render-only v1 (`<a href>` / Pango link markup); no link-activation event.
- **Qt:** deferred; Qt falls back to plain text. Status note only.
- **Offsets:** UTF-8 **byte** offsets into the text (Pango-native; DOM converts to UTF-16 when needed).

---

### 1. Protocol (spec first)

**`spec/OPCODE.md`**
- Add `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT` to the PARAMETER table: `A=nodeId`, `B=arenaRef` (shared memory) / relative string-section offset (network), `C=0`.
- Add an "Attributed text payload" section. Proposed entry (inside the arena's `[u32 byteLength][bytes]` wrapper):

```
[u32 textByteLen][utf8 text]
[u32 runCount]
  run:
    [u32 start][u32 end][u32 attrCount]
    attr:
      [u16 propId][u8 valueType][u8 reserved][u32 value]
[u32 linkCount]
  link:
    [u32 start][u32 end][u32 urlByteLen][utf8 url]
```

- `valueType` reuses the standard codes (`U8/U32/I32/F32/ENUM/COLOR`); STRING/DESIGN_TOKEN/LIST are invalid inside runs in v1.
- Semantics: node-level properties remain the base; runs override ranges; overlapping runs apply in wire order (later wins per property); links are separate, last covering link wins; ranges are `[start,end)`, validated against text length and UTF-8 boundaries.
- Renderers that do not support rich text render the payload's plain text (fallback guarantee).

 # Pathland Project - AI Agent Guide
 
 This document provides essential context for AI agents (or human contributors) working on the **Pathland** protocol. It captures the project's direction, architectural decisions, and implementation details to ensure consistency.
 
 **Last Updated**: November 3, 2026
 
 ---
 
 ## Architecture: Rust Opcode Engine
 
 > The canonical core is a **Rust engine** that emits the application's
 > **declarative view structure** — VStack, HStack, Text, spacing, padding,
 > alignment — as a fixed **16-byte opcode ring buffer** into shared linear
 > memory, consumed by host renderers. View components and modifiers are written
 > in Rust with a SwiftUI-like API, and in Kotlin with the hand-written
 > **`dev.pathland.view.dsl` DSL** (reusable JVM library, Java 17+); both drive the
 > engine through the flat **native C ABI** (`pathland-view-native`) over a
 > zero-copy shared ring on desktop. Java hosts mount Kotlin views through
 > `PathlandApp`.
 
 ### The 16-byte Opcode Engine
 
 - Every opcode is exactly **16 bytes**: `Category (1B) | Command ID (1B) | Flags (2B) | A (4B) | B (4B) | C (4B)`, `#[repr(C, packed)]`, little-endian.
 - A 64-byte cache line holds exactly **4 opcodes** → L1-cache-friendly.
 - Opcodes live in a **ring buffer** in linear memory; the guest writes at `writeCursor`, the host reads from `readCursor`; frame boundaries via a monotonic `frameCount` in the header block.
 - **Both directions are binary**: a second **event ring** (host → guest) carries `EVENT`-category opcodes. The renderer writes raw inputs at `eventWriteCursor`; the guest drains them at `eventReadCursor`. Events are 16-byte opcodes through the engine, never a side-channel callback.
 - **Variable-length data** (strings, token paths) lives in a bump **arena**; opcodes reference entries by offset (`[u32 byteLength][bytes...]`), so every opcode stays 16 bytes. A second host-owned **event arena** mirrors this in the host → guest direction (shared-memory event strings, e.g. `TEXT_CHANGED`); over the network, host → guest strings ride the batch's string section.
 - **Window metadata** (`META::SET_WINDOW_METADATA`, field family `TITLE`/`DESCRIPTION`/`LOCALE`) carries the hosting surface's presentation metadata; renderers map it to their own chrome (browser `<title>`/meta description/`<html lang>`, GTK/Qt window title). It is root-scoped and signal-backed, so a route title is a computed over the router. Web-only artifacts (canonical/robots/sitemap) stay host-owned.
 - Spec: **`spec/OPCODE.md`** (primary) + **`spec/CONFORMANCE.md`** (golden vectors). Companion catalogs: **`spec/PRIMITIVES.md`** (views), **`spec/MODIFIERS.md`** (modifiers/properties), **`spec/EVENTS.md`** (events), **`spec/LAYOUT.md`** (frame & layout allocation contract) — draft IDs are allocated there spec-first.
 
 ### Declarative, not positioned (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
 > **The engine describes WHAT the UI is — VStack, HStack, Text, spacing,
 > padding, alignment — never WHERE it is. It does not compute layout and does
 > not emit rects.**
 
 - The engine emits **declarative structure** (`TREE` create/delete/insert/remove/move) + **constraint properties** (`PARAMETER` spacing/padding/alignment/FILL/HUG hints).
 - **Native elements everywhere**: each platform's renderer maps the opcode stream onto that platform's native elements — GTK4 widgets on desktop, DOM elements in the browser, HTML server-side — and those native elements lay themselves out. Never a generic canvas unless a platform has no native equivalent.
 - **Reactive emission**: emission is diff-based. Only the nodes that changed emit opcodes (property diffs via `SET_PROPERTY`/`SET_TEXT`, structural diffs via `TREE` opcodes). An unchanged tree emits **zero** opcodes. Signals in the application mark the tree dirty; the engine reconciles.
 - **Zero dynamic heap allocations** during steady-state emission (proven by test).
 
 ### no_std / wasm32 direction guard (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
 `pathland-core` and `pathland-view` must remain `#![no_std]` + `alloc` and
 compile for `wasm32-unknown-unknown`. This is the guarantee that the protocol
 core can still target a browser / embedded / remote projection later (goal #15,
 Quarkus SSR + WebSocket). The desktop path (`pathland-view-native`) is the only
 consumer today, but the core must not become desktop-only. Verify with
 `lib/rust/check-wasm.sh` (i.e. `cargo build -p pathland-core -p pathland-view
 --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`).
 
 ### Reactive signals (Angular-style)
 
 `pathland-core::signal` provides writable signals that live in the engine. A
 node binds its text (`Node::text_binding`), a property
 (`Node::property_bindings`) or a **string property** (`Node::string_bindings`,
 e.g. a media controller's `MEDIA_SOURCE`) to a `SignalId`; during emit the engine
 resolves the binding and records the dependency, and `Engine::set_signal`
 re-emits **only the bound nodes** (`SET_TEXT` / `SET_PROPERTY`) — no full tree
 walk. Signal values
 are one of `F32`/`U32`/`Bool`/`Enum`/`Str` (packed to the wire's `u32` value or
 arena string). Foreign hosts reach signals via the flat C ABI
 (`pathland_native_signal_create_*` / `signal_set_*` / `node_bind_text` /
 `node_bind_property`) and the Kotlin/JVM `Signal` type. Binding then calling `emit`
 records the dependency; a subsequent `set` is a partial emit. (Computed/derived
 signals + effects are the planned next step.)

 ### HTML base design (`design/`)
 
 The HTML renderer's built-in stylesheet is generated from a **three-layer Style
 Dictionary pipeline** plus hand-authored reset/component CSS (one built-in base
 design; no app-facing base-design selection):
 
 ```
 design/tokens/base/*.tokens.json      # internal palette + scales (not emitted)
 design/tokens/semantic/*.tokens.json  # protocol catalog semantics (emitted)
 design/tokens/component/*.tokens.json # per-component surface (emitted)
 design/html/{reset,components}.css    # hand-authored CSS consuming var(--pl-*)
 design/scripts/{build,dev,check}.mjs  # SD build, watcher/preview, validation
 design/build/base.css                 # generated: reset + tokens + components
 design/build/base.css.name            # content hash: base-<sha256-12>.css
 ```
 
 - Tokens are flat DTCG entries (`$value`/`$type`/`$extensions.pathland`) because
   the catalog has both leaf and group paths (`control.border` vs
   `control.border.width`). Dark values live on `$extensions.pathland.dark`;
   durations/z-index/`em` icon sizes are marked internal.
 - `npm --prefix design run build` generates
   `design/build/{tokens.css,manifest.json,base.css,base.css.name}`;
   `npm --prefix design run check` validates catalog coverage, layer direction,
   dark/forced-dark declarations, dimension/`isLengthToken` rules, and the CSS
   content hash.
 - `scripts/sync-design-css.sh` copies the bundle + name to
   `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/assets/` (committed; `--check` fails on
   drift). `css.rs` embeds both with `include_str!` (`builtin_css()` /
   `builtin_css_name()`).
 - The renderer's library default is inline (`render_document`); the linked mode
   (`render_document_linked`, C ABI `pathland_html_render_linked` +
   `pathland_html_base_css[_name]`, Java `renderLinked`/`baseCss`/`baseCssName`)
   emits `{base}/base-<hash>.css`. The Spring Boot and Quarkus starters use it
   and serve the renderer-owned bytes immutable (global + mounted bases); token
   overrides/fit rules stay inline.
 - `scripts/lib.sh` (`build_rust_html`), the Maven `refresh-ide` profile, and CI
   run the design build + sync. Do not edit generated CSS by hand.
 
 ### Native C-ABI shim (`pathland-view-native` + `pathland-core-capi`)
 
 The **desktop/cross-language zero-copy path**: `pathland-view-native` exposes the
 flat world (the flat `builder`/`engine` surface) as `pathland_native_*` C
 functions with a **shared-memory ring** the host driver reads in place. Any
 language that links the dylib (Swift/Java via FFI) calls the flat surface —
 no per-component wrappers — and consumes opcodes zero-copy.
 
 `pathland-core-capi` (`libpathland_core`) is the **minimal ring C ABI** for the
 Kotlin DSL: `pathland_core_create`/`destroy`, `pathland_ring_buffer_push` (one
 raw 16-byte opcode), `pathland_core_arena_alloc`, frame boundaries, zero-copy
 `ring_ptr`/`ring_len`, and event drain/send. The Kotlin DSL
 (`dev.pathland.view.core.ffm`) binds it with **JNA** (lazily loaded, zero JNI) and
 owns the retained tree + diff emission itself.
 
 ### GTK4 Renderer (`pathland-render-gtk`)
 
 The desktop renderer: a single crate that owns **all** GTK/glib/pango usage and
 maps opcode frames **incrementally** onto native GTK widgets (a retained
 `id → gtk::Widget` map). Both the Rust demo and the Java demo render through
 it — the demos **never call GTK or Swing directly**:
 
 - Rust demo links `pathland-render-gtk` as an `rlib` and calls `GtkRenderer::run(...)`
   with a wake closure.
 - The Java/Kotlin desktop demo (`pathland-desktop-demo`) loads `pathland-render-gtk`
   as a `cdylib` via JNA and
   calls `pathland_gtk_run_ring(ring, on_event, width, height)` over the Kotlin view's
   `libpathland_core` ring; native inputs round-trip as `EVENT` opcodes through the shared
   ring. The renderer **writes** the events and **wakes** the host (no payload); the host
   drains the event ring itself via `pathland_core_drain_events`. Events are never
   delivered through a side-channel callback — they flow through the opcode engine.
   The demo mounts the Kotlin `MusicPlayerView` (the same shared view the web demos use) with the
   app-driven media contract: the renderer plays the tracks through a direct GStreamer
   `playbin` and reports `MEDIA_*` events back; the demo's web-style
   `/_pathland/assets/...` paths resolve against an extracted local asset root
   (`pathland_gtk_set_asset_root`).
 
 The renderer maps native inputs onto the raw `Event` surface via GTK4
 controllers (`Button::clicked` → pointer up, `EventControllerMotion` →
 pointer move/enter/leave), emitting events through the same `Pump::send_input`
 path.
 
 `pathland_gtk::run` passes an explicit empty argv to GTK (the process command
 line belongs to the embedding host — e.g. the JVM's `-cp`/`-D` flags — and must
 not be parsed as GTK options).
 
 ### Kotlin JVM authoring DSL (`dev.pathland.view.dsl`, in `lib/java/pathland-view-core`)
 
 The **sole JVM authoring surface**. It is the SwiftUI-like DSL shared by desktop,
 Spring Boot, Quarkus, and web apps. Components and modifiers:
 
 - `View` is an **open Kotlin interface** — the library ships `Text`/`Image`/`Color`/
   `Rectangle`, `VStack`/`HStack`/`ZStack`, `Spacer`, `Button`,
   `TextField(placeholder, WritableSignal<String>)`, `Video` (a
   `MediaController`'s surface), and application code defines its own views by
   extending `Component` or implementing `View`. **Media is a state object, not a
   view** (spec/MEDIA.md): `MediaController` owns the resource + transport as
   signals, a `Video` surface renders it, and **audio has no view** — the app
   binds its own buttons/sliders (`controller.attach()` materializes the
   controller's node once, outside any swapping branch).
 - **SwiftUI-style `body()` / reactive components**: composite views declare
   `View body()`; a signal read there subscribes that component, and a later write
   re-renders only that component and diffs its retained subtree. A signal bound
   to a node stays fine-grained and does not re-run the body. Plain
   `if`/`when`/`for` works; `ForEach` is the reactive list component.
 - **Builders and modifiers**: `VStack(spacing = 8f) { … }`, `Text("hi")`,
   `Button("Save") { … }`, `.padding`, `.frame`, `.fontSize`, `.background`,
   `.buttonStyle(BorderedButtonStyle)`, `.windowMetadata`, navigation intents, and
   the full modifier vocabulary. Styles are Kotlin values
   (`PlainButtonStyle`, `BorderedButtonStyle`, label styles, `NativeVideoStyle`).
 - **Builder scopes**: view blocks take a `PathlandScope` receiver. `PathlandScope`,
   `Navigation.Builder`, and modifier/style `Config` receivers share the
   `@PathlandDsl` marker, so an outer router/config receiver cannot be captured
   implicitly inside a nested view block (compile-time guard only; the
   thread-local `ViewScopes` stack still collects children).
 - **Persisted state**: `Component` provides `val count by state(0)` (auto-keyed
   by property name) or `state(0, "key")`, bound to the session's
   `PersistentState` before the first `body()` render — no annotation processor or
   kapt.
 - **Java hosting**: Java Spring Boot/Quarkus apps remain first-class hosts. A
   Java `PathlandApp` bean returns a Kotlin `View`
   (`return () -> MusicPlayerView.make();`); no Kotlin compiler or authoring DSL is
   needed in the host module. Every reusable Kotlin root exposes a public
   constructor or `@JvmStatic make(...)` factory with Java-friendly types.
 - **Consistency** with `pathland_core::constants` is enforced by the
   emitter/HTML tests (golden byte layout + round-trips).

 ## Project Vision
 
 **Pathland is a cross-platform, cross-language UI protocol** that enables retained-mode UI development with multiple renderer backends. It is **protocol-first**, meaning the protocol specification is the source of truth, not any particular implementation.
 
 **Primary Goal**: Write once, run anywhere - Enable UI code to be written once and deployed across web, mobile, desktop, and embedded platforms through different renderer implementations.
 
 **Status**: The Rust opcode engine (16-byte opcode, ring buffer, arena, diff-based reactive emission) is implemented and tested (`cargo test`). See the Architecture section above.
 
 ---
 
 ## CRITICAL ARCHITECTURAL PRINCIPLES
 
 ### Principle 1: Renderer Statelessness (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
 > **The renderer MUST NOT retain application state.**
 
 - Renderers are **pure functions** of the opcode stream: same opcodes → same output
 - A renderer MAY retain its **rendered-output tree** (id → native element + computed layout) for drawing, hit-testing, and event routing — this is a cache of its own output, not state
 - The renderer MUST NOT retain component property values as business state, application control flow, or anything the application can change without emitting an opcode
 - The application owns the canonical retained UI tree
 - The engine emits **deltas only**; the renderer applies them to its native elements
 
 **Violation of this principle is a bug, not a feature.**
 
 ### Principle 2: Command-Based Protocol (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
 > **The protocol transmits tree mutations as a stream of commands, NOT as serialized trees.**
 
 - Each frame is a **batch of delta commands** describing changes
 - Only **actual changes** are transmitted (diff-based reactive emission)
 - Protocol acts like a **VM instruction stream** / ABI
 - Deterministic, linear decoding without schema lookup or reflection
 
 ### Principle 3: Binary Protocol (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
 > **The protocol MUST be binary.**
 
 - Open-source, cross-platform binary format
 - Fixed **16-byte instructions** in a ring buffer shared with the host via linear memory
 - Custom instruction-based bytecode, not schema-driven serialization
 - **Both directions are binary**: tree mutations (app → renderer) AND raw-input events (renderer → app) share the same instruction format, so the wire is language- and platform-agnostic

 ### Opcode Format
 
 Every opcode is exactly 16 bytes:
 
 ```
 [Category: u8][Command: u8][Flags: u16][A: u32][B: u32][C: u32]
 ```
 
 See `spec/OPCODE.md` for the full format, ring buffer, arena, and frame lifecycle.
 
 ### Machine-readable protocol manifest
 
 `spec/protocol.tsv` is the target-neutral ID manifest emitted from
 `pathland_core::constants` by `pathland-protocol-manifest` (`cargo run -p
 pathland-protocol-manifest`). It contains only `kind`, `group`, `name`, and
 `value`; each language binding keeps its own representation and validates or
 reads the manifest. There is no Rust→JVM source generation.
 
 The JVM mirror is hand-written and checked by
 `pathland-view-core/src/test/java/.../ProtocolManifestTest`: every manifest row
 must match a Java constant, no extra public numeric constants may exist, and
 `ValueTypes.forProperty` must match `property_value_type`. CI regenerates the
 manifest from Rust and fails on drift.
 
 Engine behavior beyond individual opcodes is specified in `spec/ENGINE.md` and
 enforced by shared self-contained frame traces under `spec/engine-traces/`.
 `pathland-engine-golden` emits them from the Rust engine and the JVM
 `EngineTraceTest` compares its encoded frames byte-for-byte.
 
 ### Categories
 
 | Category | Value | Direction | Description |
 |----------|-------|-----------|-------------|
 | TREE | 0x01 | Guest → Host | Node create/delete/insert/remove/move |
 | PARAMETER | 0x02 | Guest → Host | Constraint properties (spacing, padding, …), design tokens |
 | EVENT | 0x03 | Host → Guest | Raw inputs: pointer down/move/up, key down/up |

 ### Key Property IDs
 
 **Stack**: SPACING=0x0001, ALIGNMENT=0x0002, CONTENT_MARGINS=0x0005  
 **Text**: TEXT=0x000A, TEXT_ALIGNMENT=0x000C, LINE_LIMIT=0x000B, TRUNCATION_MODE=0x000D

 ### Colors
 
 - Literal colors are **sRGB** with D65 white point, packed as `0xAARRGGBB`
 - A color property may instead carry a `DESIGN_TOKEN` reference to a token path
 - Semantic token resolution and theme adaptation are **renderer-owned**
 
 ### Design Token System
 
 **Core Principle**: Application defines intent, overrides, and the theme.
 Renderer defines visual appearance, behavior, defaults, and interaction states.
 
 - The **application owns the theme**: token overrides (base = **light**, `dark.`-prefixed = **dark**) and token references in style properties. Token refs cover COLOR and non-color values (`Length` for spacing/padding/font size/radius/border/frame; `FontFamily.Token` for STRING) in the Rust and Kotlin DSLs.
 - The **renderer owns** default token values (light + dark, the full Tier-1 catalog), token resolution (including explicit `dark.` = forced dark and parent fallback), effective color-scheme detection, interaction states (hover, pressed, focus, disabled), and theme adaptation
 - `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` identifies tokens by **dot-separated string paths** (e.g. `color.primary`, `space.2`) with the standard value-type encoding — there is no separate numeric tokenId system. A `dark.` prefix selects the dark variant (`dark.color.primary`); a `DESIGN_TOKEN` reference whose path starts with `dark.` forces the dark value in either scheme
 - **Runtime theming**: `META::RESET_THEME` clears every app override; a replacement theme is reset + `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` overrides in one frame. `META::SET_COLOR_SCHEME` forces `platform`/`light`/`dark`. Both are renderer state — no node is re-emitted. Java: `Emitter.replaceTheme`/`setColorScheme` + `PathlandSession.setTheme`/`setColorScheme`; Rust: `Engine::reset_theme`/`set_color_scheme`.
 - An unresolvable token reference leaves the property **unset** (renderer default), never an error or stale value.
 - The protocol MUST NEVER describe hover styles, click styles, visual transitions, conditional styling, or layout tuning for interaction states
 - **Deferred**: applying per-component tokens to native GTK/Qt leaf control chrome; web parent-path fallback.
 
 The HTML renderer's default token values are generated from `design/` (see
 "HTML base design" above). Full details: [Design Token System](./spec/OPCODE.md#design-token-system)
 and the canonical catalog / color-scheme contract in [spec/TOKENS.md](./spec/TOKENS.md).
 
 ---
 
 ## Implementation Guidelines
 
 ### Adding New Component
 1. Add to `component_type` in `lib/rust/crates/pathland-core/src/constants.rs`
 2. Document in `spec/OPCODE.md`
 3. Implement the component type in `pathland-core` (if it affects the retained tree)
 4. Implement native-element mapping in the target renderer (Goal 3–5)
 5. Update the affected project(s)' `status.md`
 
 ### Adding New Property
 1. Add to the appropriate property module in `constants.rs`
 2. Document in `spec/OPCODE.md`
 3. Handle the value type in `pathland-core`'s diff emission (if a stack/text/size property)
 4. Implement in each renderer's property application
 5. Update the affected project(s)' `status.md`
 
 ### Modifying Protocol
 1. Update `spec/OPCODE.md` first (and `spec/CONFORMANCE.md` vectors)
 2. Update `constants.rs` and `pathland-core` encoding/emitters
 3. Run `cd lib/rust && cargo run -p pathland-protocol-manifest` and commit the
    updated `spec/protocol.tsv`
 4. Update the hand-written JVM protocol constants (the Java manifest test fails
    with the exact missing/stale row otherwise)
 5. If emission behavior changed, run
    `cargo run -p pathland-engine-golden -- --emit` and commit the trace fixtures
 6. Verify backward compatibility; update `pathland-core`/renderers + tests
 7. Update the affected project(s)' `status.md`
 
 ### Changing the Wire Format
 - Bump the wire `version` field in `spec/OPCODE.md` and `pathland-core`'s header (currently 1). Pre-release format changes are acceptable while version stays 1.
 
 ### Keeping implementation status updated (MANDATORY)
 
 **The agent MUST keep the per-project `status.md` files in sync with the code.**
 Whenever you land a protocol or renderer change — a new component/property/
 command/event, a new encoder/decoder, a new widget mapping, a new modifier or
 renderer feature, a test that proves new surface — **update the affected
 project's `status.md`** (Implemented / Not implemented / gaps) in the same
 change. The specs (`spec/`) describe the protocol contract only and MUST NOT
 carry implementation status; status lives in `status.md` next to each
 implementing project.
 
 ---
 
 ## Common Pitfalls
 
 ### NEVER Do These
 | Anti-Pattern | Why Wrong | Correct |
 |--------------|-----------|---------|
 | Renderer stores application state | Violates statelessness | Application owns the tree |
 | Engine computes layout / emits rects | Violates declarative model | Emit structure + constraints; native elements lay out |
 | Send full trees | Inefficient | Diff-based reactive emission |
 | String property names | Larger payloads | Use numeric IDs |
 | String component names | Larger payloads | Use numeric IDs |
 | Generic RGB | Ambiguous | Explicitly sRGB |
 | Hover styles in protocol | Renderer job | Define in theme |
 | Heap allocation in steady-state emission | Slow | Preallocated snapshot slab + arena |

 ## Quick Start
 
 1. Read this file, `spec/OPCODE.md`, and `spec/ENGINE.md`
 2. Run Rust tests: `cd lib/rust && cargo test` (runs all crates)
 3. Build/test the JVM libraries: `cd lib/java && mvn install`
 4. Make small changes, verify they work
 
 ---
 
 ## Pathland Mindset
 
 **Always remember**:
 1. Protocol is King
 2. Renderers are Dumb (execute commands only)
 3. Applications are Smart (generate commands)
 4. Only Changes Matter (transmit mutations / reactive emission)
 5. Binary is Beautiful (efficient, deterministic)
 
 **When in doubt**: Check `spec/OPCODE.md`, the conformance vectors in `spec/CONFORMANCE.md`, and the companion catalogs (`spec/PRIMITIVES.md`, `spec/MODIFIERS.md`, `spec/EVENTS.md`, `spec/LAYOUT.md`), and the reference implementation (`pathland-core`). Ask: "Does this maintain stateless renderers?" "Does this only transmit actual changes?" "Does this describe WHAT the UI is, never WHERE?" "Is this representable as a 16-byte opcode in any language?"

+# pathland-markdown (Java) — implementation status
+
+**Last updated:** November 6, 2026
+
+The Java binding to the shared Rust Markdown parser (`dev.pathland.markdown`).
+A JNA shim over `libpathland_markdown`; the jar embeds the cdylib under
+`META-INF/native/` (the `pathland-render-html` pattern).
+
+## Implemented
+
+- `Markdown.parse(String): AttributedString` — the same inline parser the Rust
+  DSL uses; results decode into the pure-Java `dev.pathland.view.core.AttributedString`.
+- `Markdown.isAvailable()` for graceful degradation when the native library is
+  absent (the test suite skips).
+- Native resolution: `pathland.markdown.lib` override → jar-embedded dylib →
+  local Rust debug build → `java.library.path`.
+- `mvn` `process-resources` embeds the host build or the staged release natives.
+
+## Not implemented / gaps
+
+- The module is not yet listed in the demo app dependencies; apps opt in by
+  adding `dev.pathland:pathland-markdown` when they want `Markdown.parse`.
+- Block-level Markdown is not supported (it shares the inline parser).

The **sender runs OUTSIDE the monitor** — a blocking/queueing send can never stall the actor thread's `append` or the flush scheduler. This module also ships the `dev.pathland.observability` Micrometer + OpenTelemetry adapters; the starters auto-wire them. Logging is **SLF4J** (both frameworks bind it) — the old ad-hoc `System.out` is gone. Pure + unit-tested. - **`proxy.ProxyTransport`** + **`proxy.JdkWebSocketTransport`** — the outbound connection seam (default: the JDK `HttpClient` WebSocket client, no new dependency) with a `Factory` so a starter can swap a native client. - **`proxy.ProxySession`** — one origin connection: sends `META::ENVIRONMENT` + `META::RESYNC`, **remaps** the origin snapshot into the proxy's block and attaches the origin root under the proxy node, forwards live deltas remapped, routes client events back (target unmapped), replies `PONG` to origin `PING`, translates origin `META::RESET` into a **scoped** subtree teardown (never a global reset), tears the subtree down on disconnect (the origin session is per-connection), and reconnects with exponential backoff. The host's frames feed the session's `DeltaBatcher` (a single unified sequence); `dispatch` splits proxy-range events to the origin and everything else to the app's own bindings; `close` tears the proxies down. `proxyTransportFactory(...)` lets a host supply a framework transport. - **`PathlandTelemetry`** — `proxyConnected`/`proxyDisconnected`/`proxyBatchDropped`/ `proxyResyncRequested` (all default no-ops). **SSR embed (M2).** `renderHtml` starts the proxies and **blocks** for each origin's snapshot (`ProxySession.awaitSnapshot`, bounded by a 2s timeout), then splices the remapped origin frames into the session's mount frame (`FrameMerger`, reusing the batcher's string rebasing via `FrameRebase`) so the renderer emits **one** document — the origin subtree plus its fit band rules in the same head. The origin's **global** token overrides (`SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`) are **dropped** (live + SSR): a proxied app renders under the **host's** theme, while its token *references* resolve against that theme (spec/PROXY.md §9). A proxy whose origin does not answer in time renders empty (a placeholder) and hydrates over the live connection. A client `META::RESYNC` also replays A's tree **and** asks every origin for a fresh snapshot (`ProxyHost.resyncAll`). **Gaps (M3):** nested proxies and per-proxy theme scoping are deferred (the origin's global overrides are dropped, not scoped, spec/PROXY.md §9). --- lib/java/pathland-view-core/src/main/kotlin/dev/pathland/view/core/AttributedString.kt

+package dev.pathland.view.core
+
+import dev.pathland.view.core.protocol.Properties
+import dev.pathland.view.core.protocol.ValueTypes
+import java.io.ByteArrayOutputStream
+import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets
+
+/**
+ * A scalar text-format attribute on a range.
+ *
+ * [value] is the standard 4-byte wire value (an `F32` bit pattern for float
+ * attributes, a packed `0xAARRGGBB` for colors, `0`/`1` for booleans).
+ */
+data class TextAttribute(
+    val property: Int,
+    val valueType: Int = ValueTypes.forProperty(property),
+    val value: Int,
+) {
+    companion object {
+        @JvmStatic fun fontSize(points: Float) =
+            TextAttribute(Properties.FONT_SIZE, ValueTypes.F32, points.toRawBits())
+
+        @JvmStatic fun fontWeight(weight: Float) =
+            TextAttribute(Properties.FONT_WEIGHT, ValueTypes.F32, weight.toRawBits())
+
+        @JvmStatic fun color(argb: Int) =
+            TextAttribute(Properties.COLOR, ValueTypes.COLOR, argb)
+
+        @JvmStatic fun italic() =
+            TextAttribute(Properties.FONT_STYLE, ValueTypes.F32, 1.0f.toRawBits())
+
+        @JvmStatic fun fontDesign(code: Int) =
+            TextAttribute(Properties.FONT_DESIGN, ValueTypes.F32, code.toFloat().toRawBits())
+
+        @JvmStatic fun underline(on: Boolean = true) =
+            TextAttribute(Properties.UNDERLINE, ValueTypes.U8, if (on) 1 else 0)
+
+        @JvmStatic fun strikethrough(on: Boolean = true) =
+            TextAttribute(Properties.STRIKETHROUGH, ValueTypes.U8, if (on) 1 else 0)
+    }
+}
+
+/** A range of the text with a set of scalar attributes (UTF-8 byte offsets). */
+data class StyleRun(
+    val start: Int,
+    val end: Int,
+    val attributes: List<TextAttribute>,
+) {
+    fun bold() = copy(attributes = attributes + TextAttribute.fontWeight(700f))
+    fun italic() = copy(attributes = attributes + TextAttribute.italic())
+    fun monospaced() = copy(attributes = attributes + TextAttribute.fontDesign(3))
+    fun strikethrough() = copy(attributes = attributes + TextAttribute.strikethrough())
+    fun underline() = copy(attributes = attributes + TextAttribute.underline())
+
+    companion object {
+        @JvmStatic fun of(start: Int, end: Int) = StyleRun(start, end, emptyList())
+    }
+}
+
+/** A range of the text that is a hyperlink (UTF-8 byte offsets). */
+data class LinkRun(val start: Int, val end: Int, val url: String)
+
+/**
+ * Text plus range-scoped style runs and links — the app-side model for
+ * `PARAMETER::SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT`.
+ *
+ * Ranges are **UTF-8 byte offsets** (the wire convention). The [Builder] takes
+ * Kotlin character indices and converts them at [Builder.build]; markdown
+ * payloads decode directly into byte offsets.
+ */
+class AttributedString private constructor(
+    val text: String,
+    val runs: List<StyleRun>,
+    val links: List<LinkRun>,
+) {
+    init {
+        val length = text.toByteArray(StandardCharsets.UTF_8).size
+        for (run in runs) {
+            require(run.start in 0..run.end && run.end <= length) {
+                "style run ${run.start}..${run.end} is outside the text ($length bytes)"
+            }
+        }
+        for (link in links) {
+            require(link.start in 0..link.end && link.end <= length) {
+                "link ${link.start}..${link.end} is outside the text ($length bytes)"
+            }
+        }
+    }
+
+    /** Encode the `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT` payload (without the arena length wrapper). */
+    fun encode(): ByteArray {
+        val textBytes = text.toByteArray(StandardCharsets.UTF_8)
+        val out = ByteArrayOutputStream()
+        out.writeIntLE(textBytes.size)
+        out.write(textBytes)
+        out.writeIntLE(runs.size)
+        for (run in runs) {
+            out.writeIntLE(run.start)
+            out.writeIntLE(run.end)
+            val supported = run.attributes.filter { isSupported(it) }
+            out.writeIntLE(supported.size)
+            for (attr in supported) {
+                out.writeShortLE(attr.property)
+                out.write(attr.valueType and 0xFF)
+                out.write(0)
+                out.writeIntLE(attr.value)
+            }
+        }
+        out.writeIntLE(links.size)
+        for (link in links) {
+            val url = link.url.toByteArray(StandardCharsets.UTF_8)
+            out.writeIntLE(link.start)
+            out.writeIntLE(link.end)
+            out.writeIntLE(url.size)
+            out.write(url)
+        }
+        return out.toByteArray()
+    }
+
+    companion object {
+        private val SUPPORTED = setOf(
+            Properties.FONT_SIZE,
+            Properties.FONT_WEIGHT,
+            Properties.COLOR,
+            Properties.FONT_STYLE,
+            Properties.FONT_DESIGN,
+            Properties.UNDERLINE,
+            Properties.STRIKETHROUGH,
+        )
+
+        private fun isSupported(attribute: TextAttribute): Boolean =
+            attribute.property in SUPPORTED
+
+        @JvmStatic fun plain(text: String) = AttributedString(text, emptyList(), emptyList())
+
+        @JvmStatic
+        fun of(text: String, runs: List<StyleRun>, links: List<LinkRun>) =
+            AttributedString(text, runs, links)
+
+        /** Start a range-tracking builder (inputs are Kotlin character indices). */
+        @JvmStatic fun builder(): Builder = Builder()
+
+        /** Decode a native markdown payload (UTF-8 byte offsets already). */
+        @JvmStatic
+        fun decode(payload: ByteArray): AttributedString {
+            var p = 0
+            fun need(n: Int) {
+                require(p + n <= payload.size) { "attributed text payload truncated" }
+            }
+            fun i32(): Int {
+                need(4)
+                val value = (payload[p].toInt() and 0xFF) or
+                    ((payload[p + 1].toInt() and 0xFF) shl 8) or
+                    ((payload[p + 2].toInt() and 0xFF) shl 16) or
+                    ((payload[p + 3].toInt() and 0xFF) shl 24)
+                p += 4
+                return value
+            }
+            fun i16(): Int {
+                need(2)
+                val value = (payload[p].toInt() and 0xFF) or
+                    ((payload[p + 1].toInt() and 0xFF) shl 8)
+                p += 2
+                return value
+            }
+            fun bytes(n: Int): ByteArray {
+                need(n)
+                val value = payload.copyOfRange(p, p + n)
+                p += n
+                return value
+            }
+
+            val textLen = i32()
+            val text = String(bytes(textLen), StandardCharsets.UTF_8)
+            val runCount = i32()
+            val runs = ArrayList<StyleRun>(runCount)
+            repeat(runCount) {
+                val start = i32()
+                val end = i32()
+                val attrCount = i32()
+                val attributes = ArrayList<TextAttribute>(attrCount)
+                repeat(attrCount) {
+                    val property = i16()
+                    val valueType = payload[p++].toInt() and 0xFF
+                    p++ // reserved
+                    val value = i32()
+                    val attribute = TextAttribute(property, valueType, value)
+                    if (isSupported(attribute)) {
+                        attributes.add(attribute)
+                    }
+                }
+                runs.add(StyleRun(start, end, attributes))
+            }
+            val linkCount = i32()
+            val links = ArrayList<LinkRun>(linkCount)
+            repeat(linkCount) {
+                val start = i32()
+                val end = i32()
+                val urlLen = i32()
+                val url = String(bytes(urlLen), StandardCharsets.UTF_8)
+                links.add(LinkRun(start, end, url))
+            }
+            return AttributedString(text, runs, links)
+        }
+    }
+
+    /** Range-tracking builder: append text, then mark character ranges. */
+    class Builder internal constructor() {
+        private val text = StringBuilder()
+        private val runs = ArrayList<StyleRun>()
+        private val links = ArrayList<LinkRun>()
+
+        fun append(value: String): Builder {
+            text.append(value)
+            return this
+        }
+
+        fun bold(start: Int, end: Int): Builder = style(start, end, TextAttribute.fontWeight(700f))
+        fun italic(start: Int, end: Int): Builder = style(start, end, TextAttribute.italic())
+        fun monospaced(start: Int, end: Int): Builder = style(start, end, TextAttribute.fontDesign(3))
+        fun underline(start: Int, end: Int): Builder = style(start, end, TextAttribute.underline())
+        fun strikethrough(start: Int, end: Int): Builder =
+            style(start, end, TextAttribute.strikethrough())
+
+        fun fontSize(start: Int, end: Int, points: Float): Builder =
+            style(start, end, TextAttribute.fontSize(points))
+
+        fun color(start: Int, end: Int, argb: Int): Builder =
+            style(start, end, TextAttribute.color(argb))
+
+        fun link(start: Int, end: Int, url: String): Builder {
+            links.add(LinkRun(byteOffset(start), byteOffset(end), url))
+            return this
+        }
+
+        private fun style(start: Int, end: Int, attribute: TextAttribute): Builder {
+            runs.add(
+                StyleRun(byteOffset(start), byteOffset(end), listOf(attribute)),
+            )
+            return this
+        }
+
+        private fun byteOffset(charIndex: Int): Int {
+            val value = text.toString()
+            require(charIndex in 0..value.length) { "character index $charIndex is out of range" }
+            return value.substring(0, charIndex).toByteArray(StandardCharsets.UTF_8).size
+        }
+
+        fun build(): AttributedString =
+            AttributedString(text.toString(), runs.toList(), links.toList())
+    }
+}
+
+private fun ByteArrayOutputStream.writeIntLE(value: Int) {
+    write(value and 0xFF)
+    write((value ushr 8) and 0xFF)
+    write((value ushr 16) and 0xFF)
+    write((value ushr 24) and 0xFF)
+}
+
+private fun ByteArrayOutputStream.writeShortLE(value: Int) {
+    write(value and 0xFF)
+    write((value ushr 8) and 0xFF)
+}

 # pathland-view-core (JVM engine + DSL) — implementation status
 
 **Last updated:** November 5, 2026
 
 The shared, framework-agnostic JVM engine, runtime and authoring DSL for the
 Pathland protocol, written entirely in Kotlin. It owns the `View` SPI and shared
 authoring vocabulary, the retained-tree diff emitter,
 signals/computed/effects, the wire codec, router, cross-platform state, JNA ring
 interop, and the `dev.pathland.view.dsl` SwiftUI-shaped builders/modifiers.
 Server and renderer modules depend on this one module; Java hosts consume the
 Kotlin-authored views through JVM interop.
 
 ## Implemented
 
 - **Protocol** (`dev.pathland.view.core.protocol`): `Components`, `Properties`,
-  `Commands`, `Categories`, `ValueTypes`, `Opcode`, `ValueEncoder`, `WireValue`,
-  `TokenPath`.
+  `Commands` (incl. `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT`), `Categories`, `ValueTypes`, `Opcode`,
+  `ValueEncoder`, `WireValue`, `TokenPath`.
+- **Attributed text** (`dev.pathland.view.core.AttributedString`): pure-Kotlin
+  model + range-tracking builder (Kotlin char indices → UTF-8 byte offsets) and
+  payload encode/decode; `Text(AttributedString)` / `Text(Signal<AttributedString>)`
+  emit `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT` through the emitter and both sinks.
 - **Signals** (`dev.pathland.view.core.signal`): `signal`/`state`/`computed`/
   `effect`/`untracked`, synchronous glitch-free flush, equality suppression, error
   caching/retry, circular-dependency detection, and a thread-safe global
   `Scheduler`. `Signals.state` binds to the ambient session `PersistentState`
   during a component render.
 - **State** (`dev.pathland.view.core.state`): `PersistentState`, untyped
   `StateStore`, in-memory store and provider. Kotlin `Component` state delegates
   bind directly before `body()`; the Java `State` field/binder machinery and
   annotation processor are removed.
 - **Transport** (`dev.pathland.view.core.transport`): `ProtocolFrame`,
   `FrameCodec`, `Event`, `EnvironmentData`, `OpcodeSink`, `FrameOpcodeSink`.
 - **Router** (`dev.pathland.view.core.router`): `Route`, `RouteTable`, `Router`,
   `Navigation`, `NavigationContainer`, `NavigationIntent`, `Params`, `Chrome`,
   `NavOp`. `NavigationLink` and the navigation helpers live in the Kotlin DSL.
 - **JNA interop** (`dev.pathland.view.core.ffm`): lazy `PathlandCore` binding and
   `RingOpcodeSink` over `libpathland_core`.
 - **Emitter** (`dev.pathland.view.engine`): `Emitter`, `PathlandNode`, `ViewSlot`,
   `RenderResult`, `InputDispatcher`, `ReactiveValues`, `DateInput`, `MediaInput`.
   Implements mount/id assignment, diff-based reactive emission, node-level binding
   effects, structural reconciliation, fit/media/navigation routing, and the
   zero-opcode unchanged recompute contract. Registered `MediaController`s are
   projected as pinned, non-visual root children; `unregisterMediaController`
   removes them without touching the app tree.
 - **Shared SPI/values** (`dev.pathland.view.core`): `View`, `ViewModifier`,
   `Configurable`, `ChildrenView`, `Modified`, `ViewBuilder`,
   `Environment*`, `Platform`, `Theme*`, `MediaController`, `WindowMetadata`,
   `ProxyConfig`, `Color`, `Length`, shared enums, style protocols, and modifier
   wrappers.
 - **Protocol manifest validation** (`ProtocolManifestTest`): the hand-written
   protocol constants (`Components`, `Properties`, `Commands`, `Categories`,
   `ValueTypes`) are checked against `spec/protocol.tsv` — including no extra
   public numeric constants and the full `ValueTypes.forProperty` mapping. No
   Java source is generated.
 - **Shared engine traces**: the Kotlin DSL tests run the mount/text/property
   scenarios against the Rust-emitted PLPL fixtures under `spec/engine-traces/`,
   byte-for-byte. The canonical order lives in `spec/ENGINE.md`.
 - **Tests**: `pathland-view-core` owns the signal, state, frame-codec, and
   protocol-manifest tests; Kotlin DSL tests exercise the emitter end-to-end, and
   the server/HTML/desktop consumers cover their integration paths.
 
 ## Authoring DSL (`dev.pathland.view.dsl`)
 
-- **SwiftUI-shaped builders**: `Text`, `Image`, `Icon`, `Color`, `Rectangle`,
-  `Circle`, `Ellipse`, `Capsule`, `RoundedRectangle`, `Shape`, `Divider`, `Spacer`,
-  `ProgressView`, `Gauge`, `Label`, `Group`.
+- **SwiftUI-shaped builders**: `Text` (plain, `Signal<String>`, or
+  `AttributedString` / `Signal<AttributedString>`), `Image`, `Icon`, `Color`,
+  `Rectangle`, `Circle`, `Ellipse`, `Capsule`, `RoundedRectangle`, `Shape`,
+  `Divider`, `Spacer`, `ProgressView`, `Gauge`, `Label`, `Group`.
 - **Containers**: `VStack`, `HStack`, `ZStack`, `Grid`, `GridRow`, `ScrollView`,
   `LazyVStack`, `LazyHStack`, `LazyVGrid`, `LazyHGrid`, `ViewThatFits`/`Fit`,
   `ProxyView`, `ForEach`.
 - **Controls**: `Button` (title or label subtree), `TextField`, `SecureField`,
   `TextEditor`, `Toggle`, `Slider`, `Stepper`, `DatePicker`, `Picker`, `Menu`,
   `ColorPicker`.
 - **Automatic child collection**: `VStack { Text("a"); Text("b") }` needs no
   `.children(...)`. A custom `Component` constructed inline in a block
   auto-registers; a view stored as a field is added explicitly with `+field`.
 - **Scope isolation** (`@PathlandDsl`): every view builder lambda takes a
   `PathlandScope` receiver, and `PathlandScope`, `Navigation.Builder`, and the
   modifier/style `Config` receivers carry the same `@DslMarker`. An outer
   router/config receiver therefore cannot be captured implicitly inside a
   nested view builder (e.g. `fallback(...)` inside `VStack { }` is a compile
   error). Child collection itself is unchanged — the thread-local `ViewScopes`
   stack still drives auto-registration.
 - **Signals**: `signal`, `computed`, `constant`, `effect`, `untracked`,
   `Signal<T>.value`, `WritableSignal<T>.value`, `Signal<T>.map`, `readonly`.
 - **Modifier sugar**: `.padding`, `.frame`, `.offset`, `.position`, `.fixedSize`,
   layout priority/z-index/aspect ratio, the full text-formatting surface,
   foreground/background/border/corner radius/shadow, visual effects, transforms,
   visibility/disabled/hit-testing, accessibility, tap/pointer events,
   environment binding, styles, window metadata, and navigation intents.
 - **Persisted state**: `Component` base class + `val count by state(0)`
   (auto-keyed by property name) or `state(0, "key")`; a `mutableState(0)` signal
   form for two-way controls.
 - **Reactive bodies**: plain `if`/`when`/`for` in `body()`; `ForEach` over a static
   list or `Signal<List<T>>` with row-scoped child collection.
 - **Navigation**: `navigator { route(...) }`, `NavigationStack`, `NavigationLink`,
   `isActive`, and `.navigate`/`.push`/`.replace` intents.
 - **Media**: `Video(controller)` stays where the app places it; audio remains
   view-less. `controller.register()` projects a controller at the root.
 - **Naming**: the composite base is `Component` (renamed from `KotlinView` now
   that the Java DSL is gone); see #174.
 - **Java hosting**: a Java Spring Boot / Quarkus app mounts a Kotlin view through
   the Java-friendly `PathlandApp` functional interface
   (`return () -> MusicPlayerView.make();`). Kotlin roots expose public
   constructors and/or `@JvmStatic make(...)` factories.
 
 ## Package boundary
 
 - `pathland-view-core` is one Maven module: `core`/`engine`/`dsl` are logical
   subpackages inside it, with a few deliberate intra-module references
   (`Color`/`MediaController`/`Modified` materialize `PathlandNode`). Splitting
   them into separate artifacts would require a node SPI first.
 - Production runtimes/renderers (`pathland-server-core`,
   `pathland-render-html`) depend on this module. Framework starters remain
   DSL-neutral at compile time; they mount Kotlin-authored fixture views in test
   scope.

 #!/usr/bin/env bash
-# Verify the no_std / wasm32 direction guard: `pathland-core` and `pathland-view`
-# must stay `#![no_std]` + `alloc` and compile for `wasm32-unknown-unknown`.
+# Verify the no_std / wasm32 direction guard: `pathland-core`, `pathland-view`,
+# and `pathland-markdown` must stay `#![no_std]` + `alloc` and compile for
+# `wasm32-unknown-unknown`.
 #
 # This is the guarantee that the protocol core can still target a browser /
 # embedded / remote projection later (goal #15, Quarkus SSR + WebSocket). The
 # desktop path (`pathland-view-native`) is the only consumer today, but the core
 # must not become desktop-only.
 #
 # Usage: ./check-wasm.sh
 #
 # Requires the wasm32 target: `rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown`.
 
 set -euo pipefail
 
 REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd)"
 export PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH"
 
 cd "$REPO_ROOT/lib/rust"
 
-echo "==> Building pathland-core + pathland-view for wasm32-unknown-unknown"
-cargo build -p pathland-core -p pathland-view --target wasm32-unknown-unknown
+echo "==> Building pathland-core + pathland-view + pathland-markdown for wasm32-unknown-unknown"
+cargo build -p pathland-core -p pathland-view -p pathland-markdown --target wasm32-unknown-unknown
